events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely
continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast
and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

weather.instruction:

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent observations.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3- 5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 2.8 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Pacific Ocean Coast. * WHEN...Through 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase this upcoming week. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re- breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday night through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Major flooding, up to two feet above ground level, during high tides is possible along the immediate coast as well as low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding of low-lying areas is expected due to high tides. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and property. A Coastal Flood Watch means that more significant coastal flooding due to a combination of high surf and high tides is possible. Coastal residents should be alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to protect property.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4 ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways on Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) combined with storm surge from large surf are expected to bring up to 3.1 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January 3rd, 2026. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. This is especially so for Tuesday and Wednesday as storm activity brings large breaking surf heights of 23 to 28 ft and adds storm surge to the water levels. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM Monday, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday, reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all- time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.

* WHERE...Areas along and west of a line from Gainesville to Fort

* WHEN...From 11 PM Tuesday to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and
unfrozen water.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 2.5 to 3.5 feet above ground level is possible Tuesday along shorelines and low- lying coastal areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Wednesday with inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5 feet. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5 feet. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM PST Wednesday. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and

weather.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

For the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 4 PM Tuesday to 4 PM PST Wednesday. * IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Tuesday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

location.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Coastal Atlantic, Coastal Ocean and Southeastern Burlington. * WHEN...From Thursday morning through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Confidence is high on at least moderate tidal flooding occurring with Thursday morning's high tide. Tide levels could potentially reach the major threshold. Stay tuned to the latest forecast for any changes.

location.region: Ocean; Atlantic; Coastal Atlantic; Coastal Ocean; Southeastern Burlington

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop.

Be prepared to begin taking appropriate action to protect life
and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency
management officials. Be sure to check the latest forecast from
time to time in case a warning is issued or any new information
becomes available.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.description: * WHAT...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Areas along Bogue Banks beaches, Bogue Sound, the Newport and White Oak Rivers, and adjacent tidal creeks, and areas in North Topsail Beach, the lower New River, and adjacent tidal creeks. * WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of vehicles will be possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting the area Wednesday evening into Thursday morning. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to bring nuisance water level rises on Tuesday across the watch area with minor to locally moderate impacts forecast on Wednesday. The worst impacts are currently forecast with the morning high tide cycle on Thursday.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 25 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Western portions of North and Central Texas.

* WHEN...From 11 PM Tuesday to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and
unfrozen water.

Protect the 4 Ps from cold temperatures: People, pets, pipes, plants.

events.description: * WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides, combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.8 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...From 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM today, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of

impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is
expected to be at 10:09 AM today, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: ...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI BIG ISLAND AND EAST FACING SHORES OF OAHU... .A large to extra large, long-period north- northwest swell build down the island chain on Tuesday. While the source low aimed its peak swell energy northeast of the area, enough was aimed at Hawaii to see surf build to warning levels during the day on Tuesday before subsiding on Wednesday ahead of an even larger north-northwest swell on Wednesday night into Thursday. * WHAT...Surf heights of 20 to 30 feet along north-facing shores, 12 to 16 feet along west-facing shores, and 8 to 12 feet along Oahu's east-facing shores. * WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, Maui and the Big Island and east facing shores of Oahu. * WHEN...From 6 AM Tuesday to 6 AM HST Wednesday. * IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make navigating the channels dangerous.

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 23 at 4:02PM HST until November 25 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
weather.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES
OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI BIG ISLAND AND EAST FACING SHORES OF
OAHU...

.A large to extra large, long-period north- northwest swell build
down the island chain on Tuesday. While the source low aimed its
peak swell energy northeast of the area, enough was aimed at
Hawaii to see surf build to warning levels during the day on
Tuesday before subsiding on Wednesday ahead of an even larger
north-northwest swell on Wednesday night into Thursday.

* WHAT...Surf heights of 20 to 30 feet along north-facing shores,
12 to 16 feet along west-facing shores, and 8 to 12 feet along
Oahu's east-facing shores.

* WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu,
Molokai, Maui and the Big Island and east facing shores of Oahu.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Tuesday to 6 AM HST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful
currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make
navigating the channels dangerous.
weather.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: An approaching storm system late Monday will bring increasing moisture and colder temperatures to the region. Overnight lows are expected to fall below freezing area-wide, allowing for isolated to scattered snow showers to develop overnight and continue into Tuesday morning. Any accumulations are expected to remain light, with little to no impacts anticipated. However, a few slick spots cannot be ruled out, particularly on bridges and overpasses. Motorists are encouraged to use caution during the morning commute Tuesday.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Significant coastal flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal flooding with up to
2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, from 6 AM to 4 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW)
at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49
AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. The alignment of high surf and high tide will increase
the combined hazard significantly on Wednesday. These
predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through
the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

events.description: * WHAT...Dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas. * WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce elevated surf with a high risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs at least through Thursday afternoon. Another trade-wind surge is possible later this week, potentially continuining the threat of rip currents beyond Thursday.

weather.description:

and call or wave for help.

* WHEN...From 11 PM Tuesday to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means sub-freezing temperatures are imminent or
highly likely. These conditions will kill crops and other sensitive
vegetation.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold. To prevent
freezing and possible bursting of outdoor water pipes they should be
wrapped, drained, or allowed to drip slowly. Those that have
in-ground sprinkler systems should drain them and cover above-ground
pipes to protect them from freezing.

events.description: * WHAT...Up to two feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas due to tidal flooding. * WHERE...Shoreline in Anne Arundel County. * WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through late Thursday night, especially around the time of high tide. * IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, water reaches the floor of the Maritime Museum in Annapolis, begins to cover Bowyer Road on the Naval Academy campus, and numerous businesses on Dock Street are flooded, along with the City Dock parking lot. weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and
unfrozen water.

Protect the 4 Ps from cold temperatures: People, pets, pipes, plants.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to slowly rise mid week, remaining steady around 4.3 to 4.4 feet through late week and into the weekend. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are inaccessible due to knee-deep water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 11:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 4.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 11:30 AM EST Tuesday was 4.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.4 feet early Thursday afternoon. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 24 at 12:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise mid week, remaining steady around
4.3 to 4.4 feet through late week and into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 4.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:30 AM EST Tuesday was 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.4 feet
early Thursday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EST.

weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

Thursday afternoon.

road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,

people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over
rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while
observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is
expected.

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

events.description: * WHAT...High risk of life-threatening rip currents. * WHERE...In Puerto Rico, beaches along the northern coastline, from Aguadilla to Fajardo, including Culebra. In the U.S. Virgin Islands, along the northern exposed beaches of St. Thomas, St. John and adjacent islands. * WHEN...From noon AST today through late tonight. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 24 at 10:03AM AST until November 25 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...High risk of life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...In Puerto Rico, beaches along the northern coastline,
from Aguadilla to Fajardo, including Culebra. In the U.S. Virgin
Islands, along the northern exposed beaches of St. Thomas, St.
John and adjacent islands.

* WHEN...From noon AST today through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: ...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI BIG ISLAND AND EAST FACING SHORES OF OAHU... .A large, long-period north-northwest swell will build down the island chain today. While the source low aimed its peak swell energy northeast of the area, enough was aimed at Hawaii to see surf build to warning levels during the day before subsiding on Wednesday. An even larger north-northwest swell is likely Wednesday night into Thursday. * WHAT...Surf heights of 20 to 30 feet along north-facing shores, 15 to 20 feet along west-facing shores, and 8 to 12 feet along Oahu's east-facing shores. * WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, Maui and the Big Island and east facing shores of Oahu. * WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Wednesday. * IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make navigating the channels dangerous.

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 24 at 3:34AM HST until November 25 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
weather.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES
OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI BIG ISLAND AND EAST FACING SHORES OF
OAHU...

.A large, long-period north-northwest swell will build down the
island chain today. While the source low aimed its peak swell
energy northeast of the area, enough was aimed at Hawaii to see
surf build to warning levels during the day before subsiding on
Wednesday. An even larger north-northwest swell is likely
Wednesday night into Thursday.

* WHAT...Surf heights of 20 to 30 feet along north-facing shores,
15 to 20 feet along west-facing shores, and 8 to 12 feet along
Oahu's east-facing shores.

* WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu,
Molokai, Maui and the Big Island and east facing shores of Oahu.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful
currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make
navigating the channels dangerous.
weather.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides and moderate surf will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood and Mendocino Coast. Up to two feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.25 and 8.75 MLLW is expected at the Arena Cove tide gauge. At the Crescent City tide gauge 9.5 to 10.0 feet MLLW is predicted. * For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and breaking waves of 25 to 30 feet are expected on Wednesday may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood and Mendocino Coast. Up to two feet of foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon at high tide. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. These impacts will include, but not limited to highway 101 near Crescent City and Hwy 1 in low lying areas along the Mendocino coast. Shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Larger surf is expected to bring more significant impacts on Wednesday.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around Humboldt Bay. events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: * TIMING: 11 AM through 4 PM. * WINDS: North at 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 20 mph. * RELATIVE HUMIDITY: As low as 25 to 30 percent. * 10-HOUR FUEL MOISTURE: 10 to 12 percent. * TEMPERATURES: Upper 40s to low 50s. * IMPACTS: The combination of low relative humidities and breezy north winds will lead to an increased risk for the spread of wildfires today. Residents and visitors are urged to properly dispose of cigarette butts, matches, and any other flammable items in appropriate containers. Additionally, exercise caution if operating any equipment that could create sparks, and keep vehicles off of dry grass. Most dry grasses, dead leaves, and other tree litter could easily ignite and spread fire quickly. Lastly, remember to obey local burn bans. For more information about wildfire danger, burn restrictions, and wildfire prevention and education, please visit your state forestry or environmental protection website. For Maryland, visit dnr.maryland.gov

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6- 8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST this morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9- 8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10 feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

location.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas

For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
6- 8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST this
morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning
to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM
Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of
flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide,
with peak tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9-
8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back
in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long
period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a
sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday.
Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10
feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by
Friday morning's high tide.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following county, Mason. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A series of storms will bring roughly 3 to 6 inches of rainfall to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow levels rising to around 5000 to 5500 feet on Tuesday, and as high as 6000 to 6500 feet on Wednesday. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow levels is expected to push the Skokomish River near Potlach above flood stage by midweek. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides, combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level today and Wednesday, with up to 2.8 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...From 7 AM today to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:51 AM today, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

events.description: * WHAT...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Areas along the southern Pamlico Sound, Bay and Lower Neuse Rivers, Core Sound, and adjacent tidal creeks, and areas along the Pamlico and Pungo Rivers and adjacent tidal creeks. * WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of vehicles will be possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting the area. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to bring nuisance water level rises on Tuesday across the watch area with minor to locally moderate impacts forecast on Wednesday. The worst impacts are currently forecast with the morning high tide cycle on Thursday.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...From this evening through late Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida, and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated flooding issues across the east coast metro areas. Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 4-6 inches of rain - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Metro Palm Beach County; Metro Broward County; Metropolitan Miami Dade; Coastal Palm Beach County; Coastal Broward County; Coastal Miami Dade County

weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County

* WHEN...From this evening through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case
(High-End): 4-6 inches of rain
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

of Cape Blanco Tuesday afternoon. Very steep and very high seas
will become chaotic 18 to 24 ft at 13 seconds. Winds ease this
evening, but a heavy long period swell builds in and seas
remain very steep and hazardous 17 to 22 ft at 17 seconds.

south of Cape Arago.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 4 PM PST today. For the
Hazardous Seas Warning, from 4 PM today to 4 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Low visibility conditions are expected.

seas. Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or
secure the vessel for severe conditions.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: There is an elevated risk for fire spread today across the Eastern Shore of Maryland today. Minimum relative humidity values will drop to around 25 to 30 percent this afternoon. This will be accompanied by temperatures rising generally rising into the low 50s and northerly winds around 10 to 15 mph gusting up to 25 mph. These conditions could support the rapid spread of any fires that ignite, which could quickly become difficult to control. Conditions improve during the evening as the wind diminishes and the relative humidity increases. Outdoor burning is strongly discouraged. Be sure to properly extinguish or dispose of any potential ignition sources, including smoking materials such as cigarette butts. Use caution while using any machinery outdoors, such as lawn care equipment, that could cause sparks to come in contact with the dry ground. This forecast considers meteorological, fuel, and land conditions and has been developed in coordination with state fire officials.
